title: Grand Theft Auto 6 is Being Review Bombed on Metacritic
description: Grand Theft Auto 6 user reviews are now live on Metacritic, but many negative scores are driven by complaints unrelated to the game itself.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## GTA6 Faces Early Review Bombing on Metacritic

The gaming world's most anticipated title, Grand Theft Auto 6, has found itself at the center of online discourse once again. According to reports from gaming media outlet GameRant, user reviews for Grand Theft Auto 6 are now officially live on Metacritic. However, the launch of these user scores has brought an unexpected wave of negative reviews, highlighting a growing trend of review-bombing within the gaming community.

## Complaints Unrelated to the Game Itself

A closer look at the influx of negative scores on the platform reveals a notable pattern. Many of the low ratings being registered are driven by complaints and grievances that have little to nothing to do with the actual game itself. Whether influenced by external controversies, platform availability, or broader industry frustrations, a portion of the user base has utilized the review section to voice grievances unrelated to GTA6's actual gameplay, graphics, or narrative design.

## The Ongoing Challenge of User Review Systems

This phenomenon places the spotlight back on how major review aggregators handle user feedback. Because user review sections on platforms like Metacritic often lack strict verification of game ownership or playtime, they can occasionally become avenues for emotional expression rather than constructive criticism. For a colossal release like GTA6, the scale of attention ensures that any external controversy quickly spills over into the game's public-facing metrics.

## Editor's Take

Review-bombing has become an unfortunate reality for major game releases. While the negative scores on Metacritic for GTA6 might look alarming at a glance, analysis shows they stem from external complaints rather than the game's actual quality. Players and observers should take these early user scores with a grain of salt and focus on genuine gameplay experiences.
